definition.next_experiment: Define a refined protocol with lower coupling variance to test for reduced noise.
definition.reason: Prior results show a positive variance delta (0.333), exceeding the prediction threshold (0.002), but the inconclusive status suggests sensitivity to uncontrolled variables rather than a robust causal signal.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate consistent divergence trends across three consecutive refinement iterations.
definition.uncertainty: The causal link between perturbation variance and outcome divergence is obscured by variance in the coupling mechanism; experimental noise exceeds signal in current iterations.

assumptions: Refined coupling constraints isolate the sensitivity of value formation to path history.
Observed outcome divergence is measurable via variance delta metrics.
Noise in coupling is systematic and reducible via parameter tuning.
definition.falsification: Falsified if reducing coupling variance leads to a decrease in observable divergence variance or a statistically insignificant result.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when subjected to identical initial state perturbations within a refined coupling regime; signal-to-noise ratio in outcome divergence correlates with reduced coupling variance.
definition.uncertainty: The mechanism underlying value divergence remains speculative; initial variance coupling may be amplifying noise rather than isolating divergence.
